rationale:
bugs_open/283, round 5 — round 4's REVISE answered objection by objection, with measurements taken AFTER the full mechanical programme ran (68 conversions + 53 page rerenders through the revised config), so several answers are fleet-evidence rather than argument. No new code or config in this round; the plan below is round 4's, unchanged, with each objection's check attached.

(1) editquality HIGH — 'a dual-active-row type could take the UPDATE on the row that is not loaded'. MEASURED: both affected types carry exactly ONE active, non-snapshot, non-deleted definition row, and that row carries the update (page-rerender: 1 row, condition contains template_changed; component-template-fixer: 1 row, query contains template_changed). Independently proven at runtime: the fixer filed 72 page-scoped template_changed items (only the new query does that) and page-rerender routed them to the sections path (53 completions re-rendered from templates; the canary page's stored render flipped and serves 34 instance-scoped ids). The failure mode the seat named is real for the four dual-row types; these two are not among them.

(2) editquality MEDIUM — 'the newly-reachable sections path carries documented side effects not proven beyond one canary'. MEASURED ACROSS THE FLEET RUN, 53 pages: pages losing all sections: 0. Pages with a duplicated slot_name after rerender: 1 — and inspected, it is the PRE-EXISTING legitimate two-instance class (idea.uk/report, generic-text-block at positions 2 and 4 with different content_data and different rendered_html — the byte-identical-duplicates index permits exactly this), not the locked-section duplication side effect: 0 occurrences of that. The per-slot shrink floor fired exactly TWICE in 55 attempts, both REFUSED safely with stored pages standing (tool-model-approach-selector/fundamentallyai.com, tool-llm-cost-calculator/webdesign.co.uk) — and both are FORKED functions (multi-row components), which is now a named investigation in 283 §13.7. Served-page spot-checks on four domains: 0 unrendered tokens, 0 duplicate ids.

(3) editquality LOW — 'the dedup's open set is unspecified'. STATED: the NOT EXISTS covers status IN (detected, triaged, claimed). A FAILED prior item deliberately does NOT block re-filing (a failed attempt must be retryable); the known gap is 'deferred', which would allow a duplicate filing against a deferred item — accepted and recorded, with alignment to workItemClosedStatuses folded into the companion follow-up item below rather than patched blind in this round.

(4) bug_historian MEDIUM — 'sibling producers keep the defect; no ticket filed'. Two halves. First, a correction to the objection's scope: create_rerender is the fixer workflow's SHARED step, so 460 fixed it for EVERY fix_type the fixer handles — repair_template_slots and the chrome fix types included; they are not left behind. Second, the producers genuinely outside this fix (StoreGeneratedComponentAction.createRerenderWorkItem in Go, and any other reason-less needs_rerender producer) now have the companion tracking item the seat asked for: site_work_items item_key='rerender-reason-producers-283', status needs_human_review, spec names the producers to audit. The reuse_agent's consolidation ask (fold the fixer's SQL INSERT onto create_rerender_items_action machinery) is folded into the same item.

(5) bug_historian LOW — 'does the sections re-render cover all slots, or could dedup swallow a second component's fix?'. CODE-CITED: rerender_page_sections loads the page's FULL stored section list (loadStoredSections, ORDER BY position) and loops every section (rerender_page_sections_action.go:376 'for _, s := range stored'); the re-render is whole-page, so a second component's fix arriving while the first's item is open is covered by that very item. The dedup cannot swallow work; it collapses two requests for the same whole-page operation.

(6) reuse_agent — 'hand-built INSERT where machinery exists'. ACKNOWLEDGED as real; the INSERT replaced an existing hand-built INSERT in the same step (the estate's current idiom for this workflow), and the consolidation onto create_rerender_items_action is tracked in the companion item rather than done live mid-programme.

edits.rationale: As round 4; applied, and now carrying a full fleet run of evidence. The pre-image-guard concern is answered by the single-active-row measurement and by runtime behaviour only the updated rows produce.

Motivated by the drain: 17 of 72 filed rerenders targeted rebuild_policy='owned' tool pages where save_page_sections correctly refuses a generic save (2 failed, 15 cancelled post-diagnosis). The fixer stops filing items that exist only to be refused; owned pages take their conversion from their owning pipeline, which has a dated pointer in its handoff.
edits.sketch: query: '... WHERE pc.component_id = $1::uuid AND p.rebuild_policy IS DISTINCT FROM ''owned'' AND NOT EXISTS ...' — guarded on 461's post-image, verify PREPARE-compiles the embedded query (the 460-lesson check class).

grounded_in: Active-row census 2026-08-18: page-rerender 1 row (updated), component-template-fixer 1 row (updated); zero snapshot/deleted interference.

Runtime proof the loaded rows changed: 72 template_changed page_rerender items filed by the fixer post-460 (the old query filed site-wide needs_rerender only); 53 completed via the sections path; canary stored render flipped 11:54 UTC and the served page carries 34 instance-scoped ids, 0 old, 5/5 data-target chains paired.

Fleet side-effect sweep over all 53 rerendered pages: 0 pages lost all sections; 1 page with a duplicated slot_name, inspected: idea.uk/report generic-text-block at positions 2 and 4, different content_data md5s, different rendered_html md5s — the pre-existing legitimate repeated-component class, not the locked-section duplication side effect (0 occurrences).
Shrink floor: fired 2 of 55 attempts, both whole-save refusals with stored pages standing, both FORKED functions — named investigation in bugs_open/283 §13.7.

Served spot-checks beyond the canary: mortgagecalculator.co.uk/tools/rate-scenarios (23 new ids), dartsonline.com/tools/setup-builder (36), robot-hands.com/tools/gripper-safety-factor-calculator (23) — each 0 unrendered tokens, 0 duplicate ids.

Whole-page re-render: loadStoredSections ORDER BY position; rerender_page_sections_action.go:376 loops every stored section — the dedup collapses duplicate whole-page requests, it cannot swallow a second component's fix.

Companion tracking item filed: site_work_items item_key='rerender-reason-producers-283' (needs_human_review) — audits StoreGeneratedComponentAction.createRerenderWorkItem and other reason-less producers; folds in the create_rerender_items_action consolidation and the dedup status-set alignment.

Scope correction to round 4's bug_historian objection: create_rerender is the fixer workflow's shared step, so the 460 fix covers ALL its fix_types (repair_template_slots and chrome fixes included); the outstanding producers are the ones outside this workflow, which is what the tracking item names.
plan.risks:
1. The 'deferred' dedup gap stands until the follow-up lands: a template fix while a deferred template_changed item exists for the same page would file a duplicate whole-page rerender — cost is one redundant idempotent re-render, not lost work.
2. The two shrink-refused forked pages keep pre-conversion ids until that investigation concludes; their templates are converted, so any OTHER route that re-renders them (with the floor satisfied) picks the change up.
3. The companion item is parked needs_human_review by design — if nobody triages it, the sibling producers keep the defect; that is the tracked state the round-4 seat asked for, not a silent one.
